Q5192110.label: 1946 Cuban parliamentary election
Q5192110.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Cuba on 1 June 1946. The Partido Auténtico emerged as the largest party, with 30 of the 66 seats in the House of Representatives.

Q4774830.label: 1984 Antiguan general election
Q4774830.summary: General elections were held in Antigua and Barbuda on 17 April 1984, the first after the country had become an independent Commonwealth realm in 1981.

Q7406510.label: 1966 Salvadoran legislative election
Q7406510.summary: Legislative elections were held in El Salvador on 13 March 1966. The result was a victory for the National Conciliation Party, which won 31 of the 52 seats.

Q1633198.label: 1996 Spanish general election
Q1633198.summary: A general election was held in Spain on 3 March 1996 to elect the members of the 6th Cortes Generales under the Spanish Constitution of 1978. All 350 seats in the Congress of Deputies were up for election, as well as 208 of 257 seats in the Senate.

Q1186734.label: 2011 Andorran parliamentary election
Q1186734.summary: Early parliamentary elections were held in Andorra on 3 April 2011 after the General Council of Andorra was dissolved over problems in passing important laws, including the budget and laws related to a value added tax.

Q4825518.label: 1965 Austrian presidential election
Q4825518.summary: Presidential elections were held in Austria on 23 May 1965, following the death of incumbent President Adolf Schärf on 28 February. The result was a victory for Franz Jonas of the Socialist Party, who received 51% of the vote. Voter turnout was 96%.

Q325038.label: Vasily Kuznetsov
Q325038.summary: Vasily Vasilyevich Kuznetsov was a Russian Soviet politician who acted as Chairman of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union from 1982 to 1983, for a second time in 1984, and for a third time in 1985. He was one of the oldest members of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union.

Q5219758.label: 1947 Danish Landsting election
Q5219758.summary: Landsting elections were held in Denmark in March and April 1947. The public elected members of the electoral college on 1 April, who in turn elected 29 members of the Landsting on 11 April. A further 19 members were elected by outgoing parliament on 7 March, while a Faroese member was elected by the Løgting on 26 March.

Q974766.label: Joseph Sprinzak
Q974766.summary: Yosef Sprinzak was a leading Zionist activist in the first half of the 20th century, an Israeli politician, and the first Speaker of the Knesset, a role he held from 1949 until his death in 1959.

Q11694.label: American Airlines Flight 11
Q11694.desc: 9/11 hijacked passenger flight, hit the North Tower of the World Trade Center
Q11694.img: Flight paths of hijacked planes-September 11 attacks.jpg
Q11694.summary: American Airlines Flight 11 was an American domestic passenger flight from Logan International Airport in Boston to Los Angeles International Airport in California that was hijacked by five al-Qaeda terrorists on the morning of September 11, 2001, as part of the September 11 attacks.

mentions.c: United States: Terrorist attack: American Airlines Flight 11

Q57527214.label: assassination of Jamal Khashoggi
Q57527214.desc: 2018 murder of Saudi dissident journalist Jamal Khashoggi on Turkish soil
Q57527214.summary: On 2 October 2018, Jamal Khashoggi, a Saudi dissident journalist, was killed by agents of the Saudi government at the Saudi consulate in Istanbul, Turkey. Khashoggi was ambushed and strangled by a 15-member squad of Saudi operatives. His body was dismembered and disposed of in a manner that was never publicly revealed.

Q58333614.label: Kevin Hern
Q58333614.img: Rep. Kevin Hern official photo, 116th congress.jpg
Q58333614.summary: Kevin Ray Hern is an American politician and businessman from Oklahoma. A Republican, he has been a member of the United States House of Representatives for Oklahoma's 1st congressional district since 2018.

Q20988334.label: Conservative democracy
Q20988334.desc: Political ideology, variant of Islamic democracy
Q20988334.summary: Conservative democracy is a label coined by the ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP) of Turkey to describe Islamic democracy. Forming as a modernist breakaway party from former Islamist movements, the AKP's conservative democratic ideology has been described as a departure from or moderation of Islamic democracy and the endorsement of more secular and democratic values.

Q11421102.label: National Cooperative Party
Q11421102.summary: The National Cooperative Party was a centrist political party in Japan.
